nodes.title: ADR-0001 — Adopt LLM Wiki as Project Memory
nodes.summary: Use an Obsidian-readable Markdown wiki as persistent project memory maintained by the LLM agent.

nodes.title: ADR-0002 — Extend Wiki into SDLC Operating System
nodes.summary: Extend the wiki with tasks, standards, session protocols, ADRs, and quality gates.

nodes.title: ADR-0003 — Simplify Folder Structure for Human Navigation
nodes.summary:
Use fewer, purpose-named folders for Echel's visible project memory and development controls.

The canonical structure is:

- `wiki/knowledge`: concepts, systems, entities, flows, and standards
- `wiki/decisions`: durable ADRs
- `wiki/work`: task artifacts
- `wiki/reports`: analysis, generated checks, and source summaries
- `docs/development`: operating files for method, work, architecture, governance, automation, and evidence
- `docs/development/state`: current state, resume snapshots, session history, decision log, and risks
- `docs/development/bugs`: bug records and debugging evidence

nodes.title: ADR-0004 — Keep Product Wiki Outside Echel Core
nodes.summary:
Generated projects keep `wiki/` at the target project repository root and place framework machinery inside `echel-core/`.

`echel-core/project.echel` points `WIKI_ROOT` to `../wiki` so Echel tools can run from `echel-core/` while reading and writing product-owned memory.

nodes.title: ADR-0005 - Adopt vNext Architecture Artifact Model
nodes.summary:
Use `wiki/architecture/` as the vNext architecture artifact surface with separate documents for overview, context map, component architecture, data architecture, API architecture, event architecture, workflow architecture, security architecture, and observability architecture.

The root `wiki/architecture.md` remains a thin compatibility page for existing graph and cockpit tooling until downstream commands read the expanded architecture model directly.
